sentences.text:
THIS MFA, COMING ON FOR FURTHER HEARING, THIS DAY,
 THE COURT DELIVERED THE FOLLOWING:
 -2-  MFA No. 20476 of 2011  JUDGMENT

The respondent No.2-insurer is impugning the judgment and award dated 23.09.2010 in M.V.C. No.
1127/2008 by the Addl. MACT, Hukkeri (hereinafter referred to as the Tribunal) awarding compensation of Rs.69,868/- in favour of the claimant for the injuries said to have been sustained in the road traffic accident.
Parties shall be referred to as per their ranking before the Tribunal.

2. Brief facts of the case are that the claimant filed claim petition in M.V.C. No. 1127/2008 against respondents No.1 and 2 contending that on 02.05.2006 at about 21.30 hours the claimant was proceeding from Ghataprabha towards Zangatihal on his motorcycle.
When he reached near the place of occurrence, i.e., Ghataprabha-Hukkeri road, the motorcycle bearing reg. no. KA/49-E-2278 came and dashed to the motorcycle in which the claimant was proceeding.
As a result, the claimant fell down and sustained injuries.
Immediately he was shifted to J.G. Hospital, Ghataprabha, wherein he took treatment.
Later he was shifted to K.L.E. Hospital, Belgaum and was treated as inpatient from 04.05.2006 till 15.05.2006.
He has spent Rs.50,000/- towards medical expenses and Rs.20,000/- towards attendant's charges.
He has suffered permanent disability.
Therefore, he is entitled for compensation.
Respondent No.1-owner of the motorcycle remained absent and not contested the matter.
Respondent No.2-insurer filed objection statement denying the contentions taken by the claimant.

It is specifically contended that even according to the claimant, it is a case of hit and run and only to make unlawful gain, i.e., for getting compensation, the claimant in collusion with respondent no.1,
i.e., the owner of the offending motorcycle, manipulated the documents with the help of Police.
Therefore, he has sought for dismissal of the claim petition.
3. On the basis of these pleadings, the tribunal framed the following issues.

1. Whether the petitioner proves that the accident has taken place on 2/5/2006 at about 21.30 hours while he was proceeding from Ghataprabha towards Zangatihal on his bicycle and he camenear Ghataprabha Hukkeri within the limits Zangatihal village rider of the motor cycle bearing No.KA-49-E- 2278 came riding his vehicle in a high speed and rash andnegligent manner from Ghataprabha towards Hukkeri and lost control over his vehicle and dashed to his bicycle due to The New India Assurance Company Limited vs Ramappa S/O Basappa Pujeri on 20 June, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/32966817/
2 which accident took place and he sustained grievous injuries as mentioned in column no.11 of the petition?
2. whether the respondent no.2 proves that the driver of the motor cycle was not holding valid and effective DL to drive the vehicle at the time of accident and as there is violation of terms and conditions of the policy they are not responsible to ay any compensation to the petitioner, hence the petition be dismissed against him?
3.

sentences.text: Whether the petitioner is entitled for the compensation amount?
If so, to what extent?

from whom?
4.
To what or award?
4. The claimant examined himself as PW1 and got examined PW2 and got marked Exs.P.1 to 16 in support of his contention.
The respondent No.2 has not led any evidence but got marked Ex.R.1-the insurance policy, with consent.

On the basis of these materials the Tribunal formed an opinion that the claimant has proved the factum of accident involving the motorcycle insured by the respondent No.2 and awarded compensation of Rs.69,868/- in favour of the claimant with interest at 6% p.a.
Being aggrieved by the same, the insurer is before this Court.
5. Heard Sri G.N. Raichur, learned counsel for the appellant-insurer.
Learned counsel for respondent No.1- claimant remained absent and has not addressed his arguments even after providing sufficient opportunity.
Hence, his arguments is taken as nil.

6. In view of the contentions raised by the appellant, the point that arises for consideration is:
Whether the impugned judgment and award passed by the Tribunal calls for interference by this Court?
7.

My answer to the above point is in the affirmative for the following:
REASONS 8.

It is the specific contention of the claimant that on the date of accident, i.e., on 02.05.2006 at 21.30 hours he was proceeding on his motorcycle while the rider of the offending motorcycle bearing Reg. No. KA-49-E-2278 came in a high speed and dashed to the claimant which resulted in the accident.
The claimant has produced Ex.P.1, the FIR registered on 02.05.2006 on the basis of the first information lodged by the informant.

Ex.P.2 is the statement of the claimant recorded by the Police when he was taking treatment at J.G. Hospital, Ghataprabha, wherein he specifically stated that an unknown motorcycle ridden by an unknown rider dashed to him and caused the accident.
Since the accident had occurred at 9.30 in the night, he could not notice the registration number nor he could identify the rider of the motorcycle.
Accordingly, Ex.P.1 was registered against an unknown person and unknown motorcycle.
Ex.P.3 is the spot mahazar explaining the topography at the scene of incident.

sentences.text: Ex.P.4 is the Motor Vehicle Accident Report issued by the Assistant RTO, Gokak according to which the motorcycle bearing Reg. No. KA-49-E-2278 was inspected on 19.06.2006, i.e., more than one and half months after the accident and he noticed that the front right side indicator assembly is damaged.

Ex.P.7 is the charge sheet filed by the Investigating Officer against one Erappa, said to be the rider of the motorcycle bearing Reg. No. KA-49-E-2278 for having caused the accident due to his rash and negligent of the motorcycle.
Even as per the charge sheet, the injured is the only eyewitness to the accident and none else have seen the accident.

When the only eyewitness the claimant has specifically stated that he had not seen the registration number of the motorcycle nor he could identify the rider who caused the accident, it is not made clear as to how the Investigating Officer filed the charge sheet against the accused stated to be the rider of the motorcycle bearing Reg. No.
KA-49-E-2278.
9.
PW1 during cross examination specifically stated that even on that day he is not in a position to tell the names of the owner and rider of the motorcycle nor could say its registration number.
He admits that at the time of filing the first information he was not knowing the registration number of the offending motorcycle which caused the accident.
The claimant contended that as per Ex.P.8 the rider of the motorcycle pleaded guilty and was convicted.

On all these materials on record it is contended that it is the offending motorcycle owned by respondent no.1 insured with respondent No.2 caused the accident for which the claimant is entitled for compensation.
10. As rightly contended by the learned counsel for the appellant there is absolutely nothing on record to connect the motorcycle in question to the accident alleged to have occurred.
Ex.P.2 makes it clear that the injured had not noticed the registration number nor he identified the rider of the motorcycle.
It is not made clear as to how the Investigating Officer who filed charge sheet against the accused referring to the motorcycle insured with respondent No.2.
It is pertinent to note that respondent No.1 and the claimant are from the same village.
Even though as per the FIR and the first information there is no reference to the accused for having committed the offence by causing the accident.
As per the charge sheet there are no eyewitnesses to the incident except the injured-informant.
But strangely the accused pleaded guilty before the Criminal Court.
There is no reasonable explanation by the claimant to connect the offending motorcycle to the accident in question.

Even though as per Ex.P.4 Motor Vehicle Accident Report, the motorcycle in question found damaged, i.e., front right side indicator assembly is damaged, it is pertinent to note that the inspection is carried on 19.06.2006, after one and half months after the accident.
No prudent man will keep the damaged motorcycle as it is even after one and half months after the accident.

11. Learned counsel for the appellant placed reliance on the decision of the Division Bench of this Court in Veerappa and Another Vs. Siddappa and another1 in support of his contention that it is a case of fraud and therefore fraud and justice never dwell together.

entities.text: Veerappa and Another Vs. Siddappa and another1
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text:
The Division Bench of this Court on facts and circumstances of the case formed an opinion that it was a case of fraud involving the motorcycle for having caused the accident but held in paragraph no. 15 as under:
"15. Fraus et jus munquam cohabitant, Fraud and justice never dwell together, is a pristine maxim which has never lost its temper over all these centuries.
Fraud avoids all judicial acts, ecclesiastical or temporal.

A judgment or decree obtained by playing The New India Assurance Company Limited vs Ramappa S/O Basappa Pujeri on 20 June, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/32966817/
4

entities.text: New India Assurance Company Limited vs Ramappa S/O Basappa Pujeri
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: fraud on the Courts is a nullity and non est in the eyes of law.

Since fraud affects the solemnity, regularity and orderliness of the proceedings of the Court and also amounts to an abuse of the process of Court, the Courts have been held to have inherent power to set aside an order obtained by fraud practiced upon that Court.

Similarly, where the Court is misled by a party or the Court itself commits a mistake which prejudices a party, the Court has the inherent power to recall its order."
12.

The said finding of the Division Bench of this Court aptly applies to the present case as the materials on record prima facie discloses it is a case of fraud where the claimant and respondent No.1 have managed to implicate the motorcycle in ILR 2009 KAR 3562 - 10 - the accident as the same was insured with the respondent No.2.
Therefore, I am of the opinion that the claimant is not entitled for compensation.
13. I have gone through the impugned judgment and award.
The Tribunal has not taken into consideration the evidence and materials in proper perspective and committed an error in awarding compensation, which requires to be interfered with.
Accordingly, I answer the point for consideration in the affirmative and proceed to pass the following order.
ORDER Appeal is allowed with costs.

Judgment and award dated 23.09.2010 in M.V.C. No. 1127/2008 passed by the Addl. MACT,
Hukkeri, is set aside.
Consequently, the claim petition is dismissed.
Amount in deposit is ordered to be returned to the appellant on due identification.
Send back the trial Court records with copy of the judgment.

SD/-
